commit_subject: fix: key QBID phase-in width to return status
description: local width mapping ($150k joint / $75k otherwise incl. surviving spouse — upstream width defect #1053)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pipeline consumed the imported statute rule `qbi_phasein_range`, whose formula `if filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4: qbi_phasein_range_joint else: qbi_phasein_range_other` handed surviving-spouse returns (status 4) the $150,000 joint phase-in width, but 26 USC 199A(b)(3)(B) allows the $150,000 width only "in the case of a joint return" and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 places surviving-spouse returns in the "All Other Returns" band ($201,750 threshold / $276,750 top = a $75,000 width).
triage.triage_notes: Single rule-module commit; the only behavioral change is filing_status 4 (150000 -> 75000). Statuses 0, 2 and 3 already resolved to 75000 under the imported rule and status 1 stays at 150000, so the new five-arm match is meaning-changing for exactly one status. The commit also drops the `us:statutes/26/199A#qbi_phasein_range` import line and its two import proof atoms (in pipeline_trade_or_business_phasein_reduction and pipeline_trade_or_business_deductible_amount) and repoints both formulas to the local rule — bookkeeping consequent to the fix, not separate changes. The commit message body is empty; the quote comes from the composing PR #1004 body, which names it "upstream width defect #1053". The companion test file (not a module, so not quotable here) adds case `qbid-surviving-spouse-uses-all-other-width` with the comment "Status 4 is a surviving-spouse return, not a joint return" and asserts pipeline_qbi_phasein_range = 75000 at taxable income $276,750; PROGRESS.md records "Replaced the imported `{1,4}` QBID width selector with a local five-status rule". I read the provision through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/199A resolved cleanly): the text says "threshold amount plus $75,000 ($150,000 in the case of a joint return)" at (b)(3)(B)(i)(I), (b)(3)(B)(ii)(II) and (d)(3), with no surviving-spouse extension; (e)(2) likewise doubles the threshold only "in the case of a joint return". The upstream statute module us/statutes/26/199A.yaml still carries `if filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4` at repo HEAD, so this fix is a local override in the pipeline rather than an upstream repair — a reviewer may want the sibling upstream commit if one ever lands. Kind could alternatively be read as amount_mismatch (150000 where 75000 belongs), but the taxonomy lists filing status under wrong_entity_or_scope and the fix is precisely a re-keying of which return statuses fall in which branch.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this and could not: the diff drops the import `us:statutes/26/199A#qbi_phasein_range`, whose formula at the parent commit (598e55889e, us/statutes/26/199A.yaml line 288) reads `if filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4: qbi_phasein_range_joint else: qbi_phasein_range_other`, and replaces it with a local rule that gives filing_status 4 the $75,000 width — the only substantive value change (0/2/3 keep $75,000, 1 keeps $150,000), so the change is about which filing-status population gets the joint width, not about a number being wrong. Read through the pinned release, 26 USC 199A grants $150,000 only "in the case of a joint return" and never mentions surviving spouses, section 2(a), 6013 or 7703 anywhere in its text, and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 has exactly three bands ("Married Individuals Filing Joint Returns $403,500 $553,500 ... All Other Returns $201,750 $276,750", a $75,000 width), so a surviving-spouse return had no source basis for the joint width. The module's own input description ("0 single/other, 1 joint, 2 married filing separately, 3 head of household, 4 surviving spouse", threshold "$201,750 otherwise") shows the pipeline already claimed status-4 coverage and was internally inconsistent pre-fix, which rules out "new coverage the module never claimed" and rules out mechanical, since a formula's value changed for a real population.
triage.verifier_notes: Corroboration beyond the module diff: commit subject "fix: key QBID phase-in width to return status", and the companion case added in the same commit, whose comment reads "Status 4 is a surviving-spouse return, not a joint return." (test file, asserting pipeline_qbi_phasein_range: '75000' at the $276,750 all-other band top). Competing kind considered and rejected: untraceable_branch (the `or filing_status == 4` disjunct has no basis in the cited text) is defensible, but the branch it re-grounds lives in the upstream statute module, not in this diff, and "filing status" is named explicitly in wrong_entity_or_scope, so that kind is the more specific fit. amount_mismatch does not fit: both $75,000 and $150,000 are correct source amounts; only the population assignment was wrong. Two caveats for a reviewer: (1) this is an intra-PR fix inside PR #1004 — the defective pre-fix text was unmerged work from the same PR, never shipped to main independently; (2) the root cause remains upstream in us/statutes/26/199A.yaml (tracked as width defect #1053), and this commit is a local workaround, so if the corpus also harvests the upstream #1053 fix the two entries would be the same underlying defect. Also note the first reader's quote ("local width mapping ($150k joint / $75k otherwise incl. surviving spouse — upstream width defect #1053)") describes the post-fix state of the whole PR rather than the defect; the decisive evidence is the diff plus the commit subject. Rest of the diff (import list entry, two `kind: import` proof atoms, two identifier renames `qbi_phasein_range` → `pipeline_qbi_phasein_range`) is bookkeeping consequential to the local rule.
